steps.explanationAfterStep: Histidine is again the general base, this time for water. The oxyanion hole holds the negative oxygen, just as in the first half.

The imidazolium ion gives its proton to the serine oxygen as it leaves. The acid half of the peptide is released and serine and histidine are back as they started: the enzyme is a catalyst. At pH 7 the carboxylic acid loses its proton to become a carboxylate.
Also correct: protonate the serine oxygen first. In the enzyme the proton transfer and the C–O cleavage happen almost together.
The neutral serine leaves and the acid is released.

title: Serine protease: deacylation
subtitle: Water cleaves the acyl-enzyme and frees the serine
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 42
Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto and Stryer, Biochemistry (W. H. Freeman), chapter 9: catalytic strategies (chymotrypsin)

products.caption: acetic acid (the acid half of the peptide) + methanol (the free serine) + imidazole + acetate: the enzyme is ready again

reactants.caption: the acyl-enzyme (methyl acetate as a model: methanol is serine) + water + imidazole (histidine) + acetate (aspartate)
hintTiers: The same trick as in acylation, with water as the nucleophile: histidine is the general base.

The imidazole nitrogen without a hydrogen takes the drawn water hydrogen, that O–H pair becomes a new bond from the water oxygen to the carbonyl carbon, and the C=O π pair goes onto oxygen. Three arrows.
Imidazole nitrogen lone pair → new bond to the drawn hydrogen of water; that O–H bond → new bond from the water oxygen to the carbonyl carbon; C=O π bond → a lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Water attacks the ester. Which group takes its proton?

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Histidine (pKa about 7) cannot turn water into free hydroxide. The proton moves only as the oxygen bonds to the carbonyl carbon.
In the enzyme histidine is a base, not a nucleophile. Water is the nucleophile.
An SN2 reaction on the serine CH₂ would not release the acid. Water adds to the C=O carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right attack, but the water oxygen would be left positive. Which group takes its proton at the same time?

protonated-intermediate.caption: the tetrahedral intermediate with the serine oxygen protonated + imidazole
hintTiers: The protonated serine oxygen is now a good leaving group.
The O⁻ lone pair re-forms C=O and the C–O bond to the protonated oxygen breaks onto it. Two arrows.
O⁻ lone pair → C=O π bond; C–O bond to the protonated serine oxygen → a lone pair on that oxygen.
protonated-intermediate.learnerPrompt: Serine can now leave as a neutral alcohol.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Hydroxide is a poor leaving group, and the protonated serine oxygen is ready to go.

tetrahedral-intermediate.caption: the second tetrahedral intermediate + the imidazolium ion
hintTiers: Serine must leave as a neutral alcohol, not as an alkoxide. The imidazolium ion is the general acid.
The O⁻ lone pair re-forms C=O, the bond from the carbonyl carbon to the serine oxygen becomes a new O–H bond to the imidazolium hydrogen, and that N–H pair stays on nitrogen. Three arrows.
O⁻ lone pair → C=O π bond; C–O bond to the serine (methanol) oxygen → new bond from that oxygen to the drawn imidazolium hydrogen; imidazolium N–H bond → a lone pair on the imidazole nitrogen.
tetrahedral-intermediate.learnerPrompt: The C=O re-forms. Which group leaves this time, and where does it get a proton?

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: In saponification an alkoxide does leave as an anion, but in the enzyme the imidazolium ion is right there: it protonates the serine oxygen as it leaves, so serine leaves as a neutral alcohol.
Losing the water oxygen just reverses the last step. Serine is the group that leaves.

mechanismSummary: The second half of serine protease catalysis is the hydrolysis of the acyl-enzyme ester. Here methyl acetate models the acyl-enzyme (the methanol part is the serine), imidazole histidine and acetate aspartate. Histidine takes a proton from water as the water oxygen adds to the C=O, giving a second tetrahedral intermediate in the oxyanion hole. Histidine then protonates the serine oxygen as the C=O re-forms, releasing the carboxylic acid and returning serine and histidine to their starting state.
